title: Alibaba launches Qwen4-Max at a lower price than the model it replaces. The Fed names AI the top risk to the financial system. Gemini can now read your bank accounts, Amazon plans a catalogue of nearly everything sold online, Apple starts a health AI study, and Meituan publishes a 1.6-trillion-parameter model trained without Nvidia chips.
summary: Alibaba released Qwen4-Max on 16 November, its new flagship, at $1.50 per million input tokens and $4.50 per million output tokens, below the $2 and $6 it charges for Qwen3.8-Max. The weights are not public. The Federal Reserve’s Financial Stability Report, published on 13 November, says debt issued to fund advanced computing passed $680 billion by October, and Reuters reports that 87% of the market contacts surveyed named AI as a risk. Google now lets US Gemini app users connect Google Wallet and, through Plaid, their bank and card accounts, with read-only access. Reuters saw an internal Amazon document describing a World Product Graph, a catalogue of nearly every product for sale anywhere, built partly to deal with AI shopping agents. Apple opened a study app with OpenEvidence that answers everyday health questions for up to 200,000 people. Meituan published the weights of LongCat-2.5, a 1.6-trillion-parameter agent model it says was trained entirely on Chinese chips.
uncertainty: Qwen4-Max’s benchmark scores and its cost-per-task figures come from Alibaba’s own tests; prices are from Alibaba’s model pages as read on 16 November. The Fed figures come from its report, which mostly reflects data as of 28 October; the 87% figure and the $3 trillion estimate are as reported by Reuters. Amazon’s World Product Graph comes from an internal document seen by Reuters; Amazon calls it a brainstorming document that may not reflect its current plans. LongCat-2.5’s benchmark scores are Meituan’s own, and its comparison table does not include the newest US models. Apple’s study terms are as described by TechCrunch and Apple.

stories.theme: Alibaba launched Qwen4-Max, a closed flagship model priced below the one it replaces
stories.changed: On Monday 16 November 2026 Alibaba’s Qwen team launched Qwen4-Max, its new flagship model, built on a new mixture-of-experts design with native vision and a context window of one million tokens. It reads text, images and video and writes text, and its API works with code written for OpenAI or Anthropic. Alibaba’s model page lists $1.50 per million input tokens and $4.50 per million output tokens, against $2 and $6 for Qwen3.8-Max, with cached input at $0.075 instead of $0.25. Alibaba says Qwen4-Max beats Qwen3.8-Max while using up to about half as many tokens, and that on its own Work360 test the average cost of a task fell by more than 60%. Bloomberg reports Alibaba claims it outperformed Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.1 and Moonshot’s Kimi K3.1 Pro on coding tests. Unlike many Qwen models, this one is not open weight: you can only use it through Alibaba’s cloud, Qwen Studio, QwenWork or the Qoder coding tool. Alibaba says smaller Qwen4 models will be released with open weights.
stories.matters: A flagship model at $4.50 per million output tokens puts more pressure on the prices US labs charge, especially for long agent runs where output tokens add up.
stories.imply: Do not treat Alibaba’s benchmark wins as settled. They are its own tests, and on some of them Qwen4-Max trails US models. Do not assume you can self-host it. Check where your data is processed before sending anything sensitive.
uses: Run one of your real, repeatable tasks on Qwen4-Max and on your current model, and compare the total cost of the whole task, not the price per token.
If your code already calls OpenAI or Anthropic, point a test copy at Qwen4-Max’s compatible API to try it without a rewrite.
Ask your legal or security team which regions and data rules apply before any customer data goes to a new provider.
stories.example: A marketing agency that drafts hundreds of product descriptions a week runs the same 50 briefs through Qwen4-Max and its current model, then compares quality and the bill.
stories.audience: Developers and teams comparing model costs, companies running long agent tasks, and anyone watching Chinese AI labs.
stories.watch: Independent benchmark results. When the smaller open-weight Qwen4 models arrive, and under which licence.

source.title: The Straits Times (Bloomberg): Alibaba unveils new flagship AI model in riposte to US rivals, 16 November 2026
source.quote: Alibaba did not make the model open weight, which would allow users to download and customise it, but said it would make smaller versions of the series available soon.

stories.theme: The Federal Reserve named AI the most-cited risk to US financial stability and flagged fast-growing debt behind data centres
stories.changed: On Friday 13 November 2026 the US Federal Reserve published its twice-yearly Financial Stability Report. In a survey of 23 market contacts taken in September and October, AI was the most-cited risk, with worries about high share prices, AI-enabled cyberattacks and complex AI-related financing. Reuters reports that 87% of contacts named AI, up from 50% in May. The report says debt issued to fund advanced computing rose to more than $680 billion by October 2026, about five times the $130 billion issued in all of 2023, and that this borrowing grew from less than 6% of investment-grade corporate debt issued by non-financial companies in 2023 to about 31% in 2026. It estimates outstanding public debt tied to advanced computing at more than $1.1 trillion. Large tech firms are also adding leases and guarantees that do not show up as debt on their balance sheets, and Reuters says the Fed found debt, guarantees and leases not yet started could exceed $3 trillion. The largest US banks have close to $1 trillion of exposure to big tech firms, data centre developers and related vehicles.
stories.matters: The cheap AI you build on is increasingly paid for with borrowed money. If the build-out slows, prices, capacity and vendor stability could all shift at once.
stories.imply: Do not read this as a forecast of a crash. The Fed says the large firms may be able to absorb losses. Do not ignore it either: it says their exposure may be much larger than their balance sheets show.
uses: List the AI vendors your business depends on, and note which are large, profitable companies and which rely on outside funding.
Write down what you would do if one AI provider raised prices sharply or cut capacity, and test the cheapest fallback.
If you invest or lend, ask how much of a data centre deal rests on leases or guarantees from one big tech firm.
stories.example: A finance lead at a software company adds a line to the quarterly risk review: which AI providers we use, how each is funded, and our switch-over plan.
stories.audience: Finance and risk teams, procurement leads, investors, and companies that depend on one AI provider.
stories.watch: Whether bank supervisors ask for more detail on data centre lending. How the Anthropic IPO and Nvidia’s results this week land with investors.

source.title: Federal Reserve Board: Financial Stability Report, November 2026, published 13 November 2026
source.quote: The complex interlinkages among firms engaged in the data center buildout, public credit markets, private lenders, and special purpose financing vehicles create vulnerabilities that necessitate close monitoring.

stories.theme: Gemini can now read your spending through Google Wallet and linked bank accounts, without being able to move money
stories.changed: On 13 November 2026 Google began rolling out Google Wallet as a connected app in Gemini for all US Gemini app users, as part of Personal Intelligence. You can also link bank, credit card, loan and investment accounts to Wallet through Plaid. Gemini then answers questions about your own money: it can chart last quarter’s spending, find subscriptions you still pay for and flag price rises, or suggest a holiday budget from last year’s gifts and travel. Google says Gemini can only read the information; it cannot move, manage or invest money, and you can switch the connection off at any time. Google’s help page says you must be 18 or over and in the US, signed in with a personal Google Account (not a work or school one), with Keep Activity turned on. For now it works in English only, and not in Gems or Gemini Live. Google also added Memory Summary, a page where you can see and edit what Gemini remembers about you.
stories.matters: Banking data is among the most sensitive data people have. Read-only access lowers the risk of an AI mistake costing money, but your transactions still flow to Google and Plaid.
stories.imply: Do not confuse read-only with private. Google’s help page says Plaid and Google both store account and transaction data while an account is linked. Check Gemini’s budget numbers against your bank before acting on them.
uses: Ask Gemini to list every recurring charge from the past year and flag the ones that went up.
Before linking, read what Plaid and Google store, and decide which accounts you actually need connected.
After trying it, open Memory Summary and remove anything you do not want Gemini to keep.
stories.example: A freelancer links one business card, asks Gemini which software subscriptions rose in price this year, and cancels two she no longer uses.
stories.audience: US consumers and freelancers, personal finance teams at banks and fintechs, and privacy officers.
stories.watch: Whether Google extends this to work accounts or other countries. Whether any assistant moves from reading accounts to making payments.

source.title: Google: Connect Google Wallet to Gemini for personal finance insights, 13 November 2026
source.quote: Gemini can only read information from your accounts; it can’t move, manage, or invest your money.

stories.theme: An internal Amazon document describes a catalogue of nearly every product for sale anywhere, partly to deal with AI shopping agents
stories.changed: On 13 November 2026 Reuters reported on an internal Amazon document for a project called World Product Graph, which aims to gather data on virtually every item for sale on Earth, whether Amazon stocks it or not. Some brands and retailers would send product data to Amazon; Amazon would also crawl other retailers’ websites. The document says Coca-Cola and Bayer have signed up to contribute data, and that Amazon held a trial summit with Procter & Gamble. It also says many answers from Amazon’s AI shopping assistant, Rufus (now called Alexa for Shopping), are factually wrong or incomplete, and that its roughly 83 million weekly searches are expensive to run; better data would let Amazon use cheaper models. People familiar with the plan told Reuters it is also meant to make AI shopping agents rely on Amazon’s data. The document lists an aspirational release date of 1 October 2027. Amazon told Reuters the document is an outdated brainstorm that may not reflect current plans, that its usage figures are outdated, and that Alexa for Shopping is roughly 97% accurate globally.
stories.matters: As AI agents start doing the shopping, whoever holds the best product data decides what gets recommended. For brands, accurate product data becomes as important as the shop window.
stories.imply: Do not treat this as a launched product. It is an internal plan that Amazon says may change. Do not assume an AI shopping answer is correct either; Amazon’s own document says many were not.
uses: Check that your product names, sizes, versions and compatibility details are complete and consistent on your own site and every marketplace.
Ask two or three AI assistants about your own products and note what they get wrong.
If you sell through Amazon, ask your account manager what product data it will want from brands.
stories.example: A small appliance maker asks three AI assistants which of its vacuum models is newest, finds two give an old model, and fixes the dates on its product pages.
stories.audience: Brands and retailers, e-commerce and marketing teams, and builders of AI shopping agents.
stories.watch: Whether Amazon confirms the project. How it gets permission to crawl rival sites, and how it treats agents such as Meta’s Muse, which it blocked in September.

source.title: CNA (Reuters): Exclusive: Amazon’s plan to own the world’s product data and fight AI shopping agents, 13 November 2026
source.quote: “Many Rufus answers are factually wrong or incomplete, but customers lack expertise to detect these errors,” the document states.

stories.theme: Apple opened a research app that answers everyday health questions from medical journals and asks people to rate the answers
stories.changed: On Sunday 15 November 2026 Apple launched a study app with OpenEvidence, a medical AI company, to learn how people use AI for health. It is open to US users aged 21 or over with an iPhone 15 or later, iOS 26 or later and Apple Intelligence turned on, and Apple aims to enrol up to 200,000 people for more than 12 months. Participants ask health questions and get simplified answers grounded in clinical sources including The New England Journal of Medicine, the Journal of the American Medical Association and Nature. They rate the answers and take monthly surveys. They can share HealthKit data such as resting heart rate, activity, sleep or lab results for more personal answers, and the app can help them prepare for a doctor’s visit or point them to a provider for worrying symptoms. Apple says the data is anonymised before it goes to a third-party cloud provider and will not be used to train AI models, and that OpenEvidence deletes questions and answers after 24 hours. It is not clear whether the feature will reach the Health app or Siri.
stories.matters: People already ask chatbots about their health at huge scale. Apple is testing, with consent and rules on data, whether answers tied to medical journals help more than general chatbots.
stories.imply: Do not treat the app as a doctor. It is a research study, and Apple says it will guide people to providers for concerning issues. Do not assume the feature will ship in iPhones; Apple has not said so.
uses: If you build health tools, compare how your answers cite their sources against an app that names the journals it draws on.
If you are eligible and curious, read the consent terms, including the 24-hour deletion, before you join.
Write down your questions with the app’s help before a doctor’s appointment, then check them with the doctor.
stories.example: A participant with a new blood test result asks what the values mean, gets a short answer with sources, and takes a list of three questions to her doctor.
stories.audience: Health and wellness product teams, clinicians, privacy officers, and iPhone users in the US.
stories.watch: Whether Apple publishes results from the study. Whether grounded health answers come to the Health app or Siri.

source.title: TechCrunch: Apple launches new app to study how people use AI for health, 15 November 2026
source.quote: Apple specified that the data will be anonymized before sending it to a secure third-party cloud provider, and it won’t be used to train any kind of AI models.

stories.theme: Meituan published the weights of LongCat-2.5, a 1.6-trillion-parameter agent model it says was trained entirely on Chinese chips
stories.changed: On Sunday 15 November 2026 the LongCat team at Meituan, the Chinese food delivery company, published the weights of LongCat-2.5 on Hugging Face under the MIT licence, a week after unveiling it. It is a mixture-of-experts model with 1.6 trillion parameters, about 48 billion of them active for each token, built for agents that work through long, multi-step tasks, especially coding. It reads text, images and video and writes text; through the API it handles up to one million tokens and writes up to 128,000. Meituan reports 88.4 on Terminal Bench v2.1, against 89.1 for Claude Opus 5 in its table, and 38.5 on the harder Terminal Bench v4.0, against 53.9 for Opus 5. The table does not include the newest US models. Meituan also offers a 4-bit version, and its self-hosting guide describes a cluster of 194 Huawei Ascend chips, with no guidance for Nvidia GPUs. The API accepts OpenAI and Anthropic formats and works with agent tools such as Claude Code and Codex.
stories.matters: A near-frontier open model trained and served on Chinese hardware shows US chip export limits have not stopped Chinese labs. For buyers, it is another MIT-licensed option that can be run on your own servers.
stories.imply: Do not plan to run it on a laptop. The full checkpoint is huge and the documented setup needs a large Ascend cluster. Do not compare it with Opus 5.5 or GPT-6.1 Sol from this table; they are not in it.
uses: Try LongCat-2.5 through its API or chat site on a coding task you already have a good answer for.
If you need an open model you control, add it to your shortlist alongside Kimi K3.1 Pro and GLM-5.3, and compare licences.
Ask your hosting provider whether it plans to offer it, since self-hosting needs specialised hardware.
stories.example: A platform team tests LongCat-2.5 on ten bug-fix tickets their current agent already solved, through its Anthropic-compatible API, before deciding whether to look at hosting.
stories.audience: AI platform teams, companies that need open-weight models, and people tracking China’s chip independence.
stories.watch: Independent benchmark runs. Whether cloud providers outside China start serving it, and on which chips.

source.title: Hugging Face (Meituan LongCat): LongCat-2.5 model card, 15 November 2026
source.quote: Long-sequence training, large-scale RL, multi-teacher learning, and infrastructure optimizations on domestic AI accelerators underpin these capabilities.

signals.raw: Alibaba, 16 Nov: Qwen4-Max, new MoE, native vision, 1M ctx; $1.5/$4.5 per M tokens vs $2/$6 for Qwen3.8-Max; cache $0.075 vs $0.25; up to ~50% fewer tokens, cost per task down 60%+ (own Work360 test); not open weight, smaller Qwen4 models to be open. New model.

Fed FSR, 13 Nov: AI top-cited risk in survey of 23 contacts (Reuters: 87%, from 50% in May); advanced-computing debt issuance >$680B by Oct 2026 vs $130B in 2023; <6% to ~31% of IG non-financial issuance; >$1.1T public debt outstanding; Reuters: >$3T incl. guarantees and leases.

Google, 13 Nov: Google Wallet connected app in Gemini for all US users; Plaid account linking; read-only, cannot move, manage or invest money; personal accounts only, 18+; Memory Summary. Not a new model.

Reuters, 13 Nov: Amazon internal PR/FAQ for World Product Graph; brand data plus crawling rival sites; Coca-Cola, Bayer signed; Rufus answers often wrong, ~83M weekly searches; aspirational 1 Oct 2027; Amazon says outdated, ~97% accurate.

TechCrunch, 15 Nov: Apple study app with OpenEvidence; US 21+, iPhone 15+, iOS 26+; up to 200,000 participants, 12+ months; answers grounded in NEJM, JAMA, Nature; data anonymised, not used for training, deleted after 24 hours.
Meituan, 15 Nov: LongCat-2.5 weights on Hugging Face, MIT; 1.6T total, ~48B active; Terminal Bench v2.1 88.4 (own); trained on Chinese chips; sample deployment 194 Huawei Ascend. New open model.
